## The miss
Both review gates passed Gerrit commit `8eadb4fbc5` (2026-08-05, "Add shrink-only C901 complexity
baseline gate", ticket `c9f7-d6df-bce0-4b77`) without detecting a contradiction contained ENTIRELY
WITHIN THAT ONE DIFF.

The change introduced, in the same commit:
- `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:64` — "``stale>0`` alone is an allowed improvement (exit 0)",
  where `stale` is defined at `:61` as a function whose score DROPPED below its ceiling; and
- `tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py:123` — `assert proc.stdout.strip() == f"active={live}
  new=0 increased=0 stale=0"`, which forbids exactly that state.

The commit message states the intended contract twice — "reductions and removed functions are
reported as stale and allowed" and "wire --check into make lint so pre-commit and both CI lanes
inherit the wrapper verdict" — so the shipped behaviour contradicts the author's own stated design,
not merely an inferred one.

## The bug it caused
`dystopian-bardlike-basil` (d319-a094-4ee7-4549): reducing the complexity of a baselined function
passes `make lint` and FAILS CI. Cost is already observable — Gerrit change 1928 lost a patchset to
a `Verified -1` across three ubuntu shards after going green locally, and its author then
deliberately reshaped the fix to be complexity-NEUTRAL (an unconditional helper call adds zero
cyclomatic complexity) in order to avoid the gate. That is the gate steering a contributor away from
the improvement it exists to encourage.

## What the gates actually did — measured, not assumed
- **Plan review: 12 sidecars on ticket c9f7, BLOCK -> PASS, 20 distinct criteria fired**
  (E1 E2 E4 E5 E6 F1 T1 T3 T4 T5b T5e T8 T9 G1G2 G6 G7 A1 COH P6 project.portability). The final
  round surfaced one advisory, `P6` ac-quality. Thorough by any measure.
- **Code review RAN** (the gate landed 2026-08-05; the earliest code-review sidecar in the store is
  2026-07-10, so the capability predates it) and found FIVE real findings on change
  `I95acf3a92b891212a42b36e72ae5fd50ce12d6ca`: a module-level `atomic_write` import triggering
  `rebar/__init__.py` side effects; `build_symbol_index` computing `name_col` differently from
  Ruff's C901 location column; an untested column-disambiguation path; an untested `_run_check`
  error branch; and a dropped supply-chain note that the gate parses version-sensitive Ruff output.

Every one of those is about whether the CODE is correct and tested. None is about whether the
POLICY is self-consistent. The review was competent; it was aimed at a different question.

## Why it was invisible — the class, not the instance
1. **Neither artifact is wrong alone.** The tolerance is correct. The assertion was ALSO correct at
   authoring time — the commit says the baseline "is generated from the live census", so it really
   was in sync. Two true statements; the defect is only in their interaction.
2. **The harm is TEMPORAL.** At review time `stale=0` held and would keep holding until some FUTURE
   contributor reduced complexity in a baselined function. Neither gate simulates a future
   contributor's workflow against a newly-introduced gate.
3. **A plan cannot express it.** The plan said reductions are allowed — coherent and correct. The
   contradiction is emergent from two implementation artifacts, so plan review had nothing to object
   to across twelve rounds.
4. **No criterion is aimed at it.** The built-in code-review registry (a11y, api-compat,
   conflict-markers, db-migrations, deletion-impact, docs, error-handling, high-critical-security,
   i18n, iac, llm-prompts, performance, public-exposure-without-auth, regression, scope-intent,
   secret-detection, security, supply-chain, surface-parity, tests) is uniformly about the code
   artifact. Nothing asks whether a newly-introduced gate leaves a workable path for the contributor
   it will block.
5. **It was IN SCOPE.** Both files were in the same diff. This is not a case where the reviewer
   could not see the other half — it is a genuine miss of a cross-file interaction in a review that
   caught five subtler mechanical issues.

The generalisable signature: **artifacts individually correct, jointly contradictory, consequence
deferred to a future change.** Every reviewer instinct — read the file, check the logic, check the
tests — passes on each half independently.

## Constraint on any proposed remedy — read before designing one
A superficially similar criterion was REJECTED by the operator on 2026-08-19: `ci-gate-compat`
("new hard-fail gates must grandfather in-flight branches", ticket `unaroused-undead-ibisbill`,
Gerrit 1919 abandoned). The rejection reasoning was sound and still stands: when a gate fails an
in-flight branch, the remedy is to rebase and fix the actual failure, so no compatibility mechanism
is warranted. **Do not re-propose that.**

The distinction this ticket rests on: there, the contributor CAN fix it by fixing their code. Here
they cannot — their code is correct and better, the gate blocks the improvement, and the only
sanctioned remedy (`--update-stale`) is maintenance-only. The open question is not "should gates
have compat ramps" but "should a gate be required to leave ANY sanctioned path for the legitimate
case it blocks". Whether that deserves a criterion, a plan-review question, or nothing at all is
undecided and is what this ticket is for.

## Suggested starting points (not a decision)
- Whether this class is better served by a criterion, or by feeding it to the existing escaped-bug
  analysis practice (`cranial-goodly-seahog`), which exists to consume exactly this material.
- Whether any OTHER shipped gate has the same shape — a stated tolerance contradicted elsewhere, or
  a hard-fail with no contributor path. A survey would establish whether this is a one-off or a
  pattern, and that answer should drive the remedy's weight.
- Note that item 4 above is a factual claim about today's registry and should be re-verified when
  this is picked up; the registry changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A verdict is recorded on whether this class warrants a new review criterion, an addition to an
      existing one, or no mechanism — with the reasoning, so the decision is not re-litigated.
- [ ] If a mechanism is adopted, it is demonstrably distinct from the rejected `ci-gate-compat`
      criterion, and that distinction is stated in its ticket.
- [ ] A survey of shipped gates for the same shape (stated tolerance contradicted elsewhere, or
      hard-fail with no sanctioned contributor path) is recorded, so the remedy is sized to evidence
      rather than to this single instance.
